title: Kling AI Pricing Plans and Cost per Kept Video
summary: Kling AI pricing is based on credits consumed per video, not a flat fee, with the entry plan at $8.80/month but real costs varying by usage.
body_markdown:
## Kling pricing versus competitors


By entry price, Kling can't be ranked against[Runway](https://runway.com/pricing) , Luma Dream Machine or Google's Gemini Omni Flash. **Each vendor meters a different unit** , and a cheaper plan can still cost more per finished clip.

### Entry price and allowance side by side


Kling, Runway and Luma sell monthly credits, but one vendor's credit buys a different length, resolution or model tier than another's.


Gemini Omni Flash is the odd one out: Google meters generated seconds of video, so no credit conversion exists between it and the other three.


Convert every plan to the same unit before comparing: one 10-second clip, in the mode you'll actually use.


Do the conversion on the vendor's current pricing page, and write down the date you checked. These pages change often, and a table copied from a review is stale by the time you build a budget on it.


In the same comparison, two non-price terms belong. Watermarks on lower tiers mean a clip may not be deliverable until you pay for the next plan up.


The commercial-use rule decides whether a clip can go into client work at all, so a plan that bans it is useless for that job at any price.


### Cost per usable 10-second clip


Compute credits per attempt, multiplied by attempts per keeper. Start with the cost of one 10-second generation in your chosen mode, then divide by the share of generations you keep.


This is where Kling's mode choice matters. A faster, lower-quality mode costs less per attempt but may need more retakes. A higher-quality mode costs more per attempt but may need fewer.


Run the same ten prompts through each vendor, count the keepers, and price from your own hit rate rather than from the marketing examples.


### When a Kling alternative is cheaper


Kling isn't the cheapest in every case. If you use it only occasionally, Gemini Omni Flash's per-second metering suits you better, because you pay only for what you generate and carry no unused monthly allowance.


Runway or Luma can win if their output needs fewer retakes for your style of shot, even with a smaller allowance. And if a vendor's commercial terms or watermark policy block your use case, its price is irrelevant.


Choose Kling when your measured cost per kept clip is lowest. Otherwise choose whichever tool is.
